mcp_config.server_provider: Same GitHub/Git MCP server as application-code -- BMAD-METHOD commits every artifact to the project's own Git repo by design (project-brief/PRD/architecture/stories are all versioned assets), so no separate transport is needed
mcp_config.server_address_or_command: REPLACE: same repo access as application-code, scoped to BMAD's conventional doc paths (typically docs/ or a project-configured equivalent)

entity_type_mapping.source_shape: Sharded individual story file (e.g. '1.1-browse-books.md'), including its acceptance-criteria section

entity_type_mapping.target_entity_type: Requirement.lifecycle_state hint (NOT authoritative -- see precedence notes)

temporal_strategy.t_recorded_source: Commit timestamp for each artifact file, per BMAD's own git-based versioning discipline -- every artifact 'from PRD to architecture to granular stories' is a versioned asset by BMAD's own design, so this is a well-supported source, not an assumption
temporal_strategy.known_pitfalls: BMAD explicitly supports human+AI collaborative PR review of generated artifacts (stories go through PR review before merge) -- t_recorded should anchor on merge time for the same reason application-code's does, not on the AI agent's draft-generation time, which may predate human review and correction.

precedence_tier.notes: REQ-METIS-CONN-05 (new): BMAD is system-of-record for a Requirement/Epic/Feature ONLY where no corresponding Jira issue exists for that item yet -- this is the realistic case for a pre-formalization product (BMAD's own workflow explicitly precedes ticket creation: brief -> PRD -> architecture -> stories, with Jira/ticket creation typically happening downstream of this, not instead of it). If a BMAD story and a Jira issue both claim the same requirement without an explicit link between them, that's a §5.3 precedence conflict -> ContradictionDetected -> Disputed, exactly like any other cross-source disagreement -- BMAD does not silently lose just because Jira is generally the system-of-record elsewhere.

notes: sprint-status.yaml is explicitly NOT used to set lifecycle_state directly (Draft/Reviewed/Approved/Deprecated, §4 of the master spec) -- BMAD's sprint/story status (e.g. 'in-progress', 'done') is a project-management concept, not this platform's own guardrail-gated lifecycle state, and conflating the two would let an externally-set status bypass Article I/II's actual gates. It's ingested as observational metadata only, cross-referenced for humans, never authoritative for promotion.
